content.thinking: The timing fits a bad deployment, but the shopper totals being short with flat metrics points more toward silent data corruption—since reverting the change would stop further drift but wouldn't repair what's already been written. That distinction between the two failure modes is the key signal here, even though a revision did land around the onset time.

hypotheses.subject: src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py
hypotheses.summary: The revision deployed at 2026-10-18T21:28:00Z stopped maintaining the month total in record_purchase(). Every purchase recorded since then has left stored shopper totals wrong. The service itself serves normally, so every request-level series is flat. The records already written are wrong and need a rewrite.

supporting_evidence.claim: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile: 240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile; the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-10-18T21:30:00Z
purchase_ledger.py diff: total_this_month_cents is no longer updated when a purchase is recorded ('The month is no longer carried')
Metrics show no departure from baseline anywhere in the window: error_rate, latency, volume, memory and cpu are all flat
The rollout converged, with all 3 replicas on 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2

hypotheses.subject: 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2
hypotheses.summary: Revision 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2 shipped changed code in record_purchase() that dropped the month-total update. The rollout had converged, so this is a fault in the released code.

supporting_evidence.claim: deployed revision 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2, two minutes before the stated onset
Rollout converged: all 3 replicas on the revision
